ms.promise:
A NixOS module that installs and configures an SPO node. At this point of development, the SPO configuration itself (and possible secrets) can be hardcoded and not properly customizable.

The NixOS configuration importing the SPO module starts, successfully begins fetching blocks, and can produce blocks manually by running appropriate cardano-cli commands.

NixOS tests verify this behaviour, with due limitations if we find out that we cannot connect to the internet from the Nix sandbox, indeed normally it wouldn’t be possible but we would like to explore possibilities given by the new “impure derivations” experimental feature.
ms.criteria:
The NixOS config starts as a VM

The node is fully synchronized

The node can produce new blocks.
ms.report:
We have a NixOS module for the block producer node:
https://github.com/mlabs-haskell/spo-anywhere/blob/main/modules/block-producer-node/default.nix
The proposed impure derivations aren't usable with Hercules CI, the alternative would be using the "effects" from Hercules CI but we chose to pursue another approach that will give us more flexibility in the future i.e. running an entire Cardano testnet in NixOS tests.
This also removed the problem of requiring secrets for running tests if we had used a public testnet together with the impure derivations/effects, and it also gives us much more reproducibility (you couln't run a test that spend the same UTXO on a public testnet).

ms.promise: A program (language to be established, probably bash, python, or something scripting-friendly) that wraps nixos-anywhere and is able to deploy the previously obtained NixOS configuration to a generic remote machine.
ms.criteria:
A “fake virtual deployment” happens successfully in a CI test.
The program works at least with a well known VPS provider.
ms.report:
We have produced a program that wraps nixos-anywhere and can deploy a NixOS configuration to a generic remote machine. This is provided in a form of a bash script wrapper that helps with the necessary arguments and allows to pass on other arguments to nixos-anywhere itself. User builds the script for a configuration named `my-node-1` with:

$nix build .\#nixosConfigurations.my-node-1.config.system.build.spoInstallScript
linking the configuration with the script that deploys it. The node keys get securely moved to the installation target machine.

EVIDENCE

-A link to a CI job running a test that verifies the acceptance criteria above have been met will be provided.

https://hercules-ci.com/accounts/github/mlabs-haskell/derivations/%2Fnix%2Fstore%2Fcj39fy0q7v98afab684fdlhhhms67gjm-vm-test-run-install-script.drv?via-job=2d6f8480-e71d-4494-b15e-96177db0feb2

Here the test runs two virtual machines and calls our installer script from one of them, deploying to the other one. Then, to verify a correct installation, we check that the newly installed machine can boot and that its hostname identity has changed. We don't test here that the machine mines blocks, but we do test it in two other scenarios in the tests: run-block-producer and [run-block-producer-accessed-via-relay-node.

-A terminal screencast showing the program correctly deploying to a Linux VPS will be provided. 

https://youtu.be/BhBe9PoVYBE

Here in the video we define a simple configuration running a cardano-node setup to produce blocks. We then proceed with installing it on a cloud server on Digital Ocean. Worth noting is that the server initially runs Ubuntu, but the power of nixos-anywhere comes from the ability of installing on a machine with any operating system or no at all.

ms.promise:
Addition of configuration options for the SPO deployment, allowing users to customize the deployment by specifying:
・paths where to mount directories used to store the states of services (e.g. the cardano-node database or operator’s keys)
・same options available for the SPO node (i.e. we would simply expose them for the end user)
・secret keys to be pushed to the target host during the deployment
・everything else which could differ across providers that we realize would need to be addressed specifically

We reserve the right to add further options according to the needs we’ll have during development.
These options will be configurable in two ways: by passing CLI arguments (or alternatively passing a “static” configuration file like a TOML, YAML or JSON) or by directly editing the NixOS configuration. The first method is meant to not require any Nix(OS) knowledge while the latter gives more configuration freedom to advanced users. 
Another possible strategy we reserve the right to approach is to provide a script that automatically generates the NixOS configuration in order to leave spo-anywhere usable by people who do not know Nix(OS).
We’ll provide at least one working example with

ms.criteria:
The deployment has been tested and verified on at least 3 different well known host providers.

The documentation contains a list of the host providers that have been tested.

ms.report:
For the final milestone, we developed a cloud deployment nix flake template, extended the documentation and tested deployment on 3 cloud providers. To finish up, we produced a demonstration video.
Flake Template - We developed a NixOS flake template for deploying spo-anywhere to a cloud host. This can be used to jumpstart a project using spo-anywhere with one command, and can be deployed to a cloud host with minimal configuration, as detailed in the documentation.
https://github.com/mlabs-haskell/spo-anywhere/tree/main/templates/cloud
Documentation - The documentation for the project can be found here:
https://mlabs-haskell.github.io/spo-anywhere/
We extended documentation to include step-by-step instructions which can be used with less technical knowledge to successfully use the project to deploy cloud hosts on popular providers. We created following pages:
Installation - This page details the prerequisites for starting a project with spo-anywhere.
https://mlabs-haskell.github.io/spo-anywhere/getting-started/installation/
Cloud Tutorial - This page is a step-by-step guide to deploy a stake pool on three cloud providers: AWS, DigitalOcean and Hetzner.
https://mlabs-haskell.github.io/spo-anywhere/getting-started/cloud-tutorial/
spo-anywhere.install-script - We added generated documentation for this NixOS module which configures the installation script.
https://mlabs-haskell.github.io/spo-anywhere/reference/module-options/spo-anywhere/#spo-anywhereinstall-scriptenable
Demonstration video
To close out the project, we produced a demonstration video that shows how to follow the “Cloud Deployment” documentation page to deploy spo-anywhere on three cloud providers.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QAAO3Rj9Opc
